 Essential tips for growing leafy vegetables during the rainy season.
 Hong Loan/Provincial Agricultural Extension and Services Center
 Sở Nông nghiệp và Môi trường tỉnh Tây Ninh • 11/10/2026 Follow Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e Add Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e 0 Vegetables are one of the province's main crop groups, with an annual planting area of ​​over 22,000 hectares, concentrated in production areas such as An Tinh ward and the communes of Phuoc Ly, My Loc, Thanh Binh, Tra Vong, Chau Thanh, Long Thuan, Cau Khoi, etc. Due to their short growing season and succulent stems and leaves, leafy vegetables are very sensitive to adverse weather conditions. During the rainy season, continuous heavy rains easily cause flooding, root rot, and plant death; at the same time, high humidity creates an ideal environment for harmful fungi and bacteria to thrive. 
 According to information from the Tay Ninh Provincial Meteorological and Hydrological Station, in late September 2026, the weather in the province will be partly cloudy to mostly cloudy, with intermittent sunshine; showers are expected in many areas in the afternoon and evening, with some areas experiencing moderate to heavy rain; average humidity will reach 84-86%. This weather conditions will cause pests and diseases such as downy mildew, leaf spot, powdery mildew, wilting, seedling death, soft rot, and various types of green caterpillars and armyworms to begin to appear and cause damage. To protect yields, farmers need to proactively apply a comprehensive set of technical solutions from the beginning of the season as follows: 
 First, farmers should prepare the land thoroughly, choosing high ground that is loose and well-drained to avoid waterlogging. Raise the beds to a height of about 25-30 cm, a width of 1-1.2 m, and shape the beds like a turtle shell – higher in the middle and lower on both sides – to optimize surface drainage, combined with a well-connected drainage system leading to the field. Importantly, farmers must absolutely avoid making the soil too fine or too compacted during heavy rains. Finely tilled soil will become compacted and form a crust on the surface, trapping the roots, depriving them of oxygen, and hindering nutrient absorption, thus affecting growth and development. Before planting, the soil should be plowed, left to dry, and limed to improve and disinfect it, limiting the presence of diseases. 
 Preparing the soil and creating raised beds helps with drainage, reducing the risk of waterlogging for vegetables. 
 You may also like Besides soil preparation, seed selection and treatment are crucial for healthy vegetable growth. During the rainy season, farmers should choose short-day varieties with compact foliage that tolerate rain and humidity well, such as sweet cabbage, green cabbage, bok choy, water spinach, jute mallow, and amaranth. Because seeds germinate poorly during the rainy season, they need to be treated before sowing. For seeds with thick shells (water spinach, jute mallow, etc.), soak them in warm water at about 50-55°C (2 parts boiling water to 3 parts cold water) for 5-6 hours, then rinse, drain, and incubate until the seeds sprout before sowing. Lettuce, green cabbage, and bok choy should be sown in seed trays first; transplant them to the field when they have 2-3 true leaves and strong roots to help them establish roots quickly, minimize losses, and shorten the care time. 
 Vegetables grow well thanks to careful soil preparation. 
 Apply balanced fertilization, increasing the use of organic fertilizers to keep the soil loose and porous. Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilization, as this will weaken the vegetable stems, making them prone to lodging and disease; instead, supplement with potassium to help the plants become stronger. To prevent rainwater runoff, divide the topdressing fertilizer into smaller doses (avoid applying it before heavy rain) and mix it thoroughly into the soil when applying as a base fertilizer. 
 To protect vegetable beds during the rainy season, cover the beds with plastic mulch or straw to prevent erosion and stop mud from splashing disease germs onto the leaves; weed regularly and prune old and diseased leaves for disposal to keep the garden well-ventilated and limit insect habitats. Finally, immediately after each heavy rain, drain the water from the furrows, then wait until the soil is dry before lightly tilling around the base of the plants to break up the crust, allowing the roots to aerate and recover quickly. 
 Regular field inspections, especially immediately after rains, will help detect early signs of downy mildew, leaf spot, soft rot, or infestations of caterpillars and green worms, allowing for timely control measures. 
 In general, to overcome the obstacles caused by rain and ensure a successful harvest, the synchronized application of technical solutions from soil preparation and seed selection to fertilization and plant protection is a prerequisite. In addition, the shift to modern greenhouse and polytunnel farming models to isolate vegetables from the direct mechanical impact of raindrops and proactively control pest and disease pressure is an inevitable scientific trend, bringing high economic efficiency and sustainable yield stability to the vegetable farming industry today.
